source: Pew Research Center Political Typology Quiz (2026 edition)
scoring_note: Each answer carries an official Pew point weight on a single left-right dimension. Positive = conservative/right, negative = liberal/left. Total score = sum of chosen answers' points. Group assignment buckets are NOT exposed client-side; see README.

group_descriptions.group1: This younger and majority White group stands out for the intensity of their views. They support expanding government services, overwhelmingly back legal abortion and LGBT rights and are deeply concerned about racial and ethnic discrimination.
group_descriptions.group2: Highly educated and relatively economically secure, they have broadly progressive political values across most issues and a deep allegiance to the Democratic Party. They strongly support the U.S.'s traditional diplomatic alliances and social safety net programs.
group_descriptions.group3: A Democratic-oriented group with relatively low expectations of the political system, they generally feel not well-represented. While they like the Democratic Party considerably more than the Republican Party, their evaluations of Democrats are lukewarm at best.
group_descriptions.group4: The largest typology group, they tilt Democratic and generally support a larger government with more services. But they have a greater sense of economic individualism and a stronger desire for order and safety in society than others on the left.
group_descriptions.group5: Defined by lower levels of interest in politics and participation in elections, they are roughly equally likely to associate with the Republican and Democratic parties. Many identify as moderate, and they tend not to hold strong positions on issues.
group_descriptions.group6: A politically mixed (though Republican-tilting) group, they lean conservative on economics and the role of government, while tilting more liberal on issues related to race and foreign policy. They prize civility and cooperation in politics.
group_descriptions.group7: A Republican-oriented group, they generally hold conservative values in many areas – but not across-the-board. Conservative on immigration, racial attitudes, sexuality and gender identity, they are more moderate on abortion, the social safety net and foreign policy.
group_descriptions.group8: Strong supporters of the Republican Party and Donald Trump, they are highly religious and stand out for their traditional social views. They also hold conservative positions across a wide range of issues.
group_descriptions.group9: Deeply conservative with a hard-edged approach to politics, they strongly support gun rights, restrictive immigration policies and a limited welfare state. They place high importance on American military power and view the U.S. as superior to other countries.
